QuestionStmt.S: If $[2p - 3r \quad q \quad s] + [3p + 2q \quad r \quad s] = m[p \quad r \quad s] + n[q \quad r \quad s] + t[p \quad q \quad s]$, then the values of $m, n, t$ respectively are

Solution.S:
Expand the left-hand side using linearity of the scalar triple product:

First term: $[2p - 3r, q, s] = 2[p, q, s] - 3[r, q, s]$
Since $[r, q, s] = -[q, r, s]$, we get $-3[r, q, s] = 3[q, r, s]$.
Thus first term = $2[p, q, s] + 3[q, r, s]$.

Second term: $[3p + 2q, r, s] = 3[p, r, s] + 2[q, r, s]$.

Adding both terms:
LHS = $2[p, q, s] + 3[q, r, s] + 3[p, r, s] + 2[q, r, s]$
= $3[p, r, s] + (3+2)[q, r, s] + 2[p, q, s]$
= $3[p, r, s] + 5[q, r, s] + 2[p, q, s]$.

Comparing with RHS $m[p, r, s] + n[q, r, s] + t[p, q, s]$ gives:
$m = 3$, $n = 5$, $t = 2$.

Thus the correct option is D: 3, 5, 2.
